messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Latency SLO breach detected for redwood-serving-shared-gpu-pool-3
incident-bot: service=redwood-serving-shared-gpu-pool-3 metric=p99_latency threshold=600ms value=1420ms stream=streaming-infer-calls
oncall: paging: @emma @raj — p99 > 600ms across 3 hosts, customer impact reported (streaming stalls). Can you triage?
emma: ack, looking at dashboards now. pulling p95/p99 & host metrics
emma: quick summary: p95 ~ 220ms, p99 spikes up to 1.4s with streaming stalls and partial chunk timeouts, correlates with NVMe write spikes on hosts hgp-03-1/2/5
raj: I see repeated cgroup writeback bursts in kernel logs around the same times. suspect IO congestion from tenant-87 heavy checkpoint writes
leo: any concurrent deploys or model swaps? deploy-bot: no deploys in the last 30m
maria: adding logs from pod on hgp-03-2 (recentest):
```
[2026-03-15T01:03:12Z] WARN streaming: stall detected, chunk send delayed 900ms
[2026-03-15T01:03:13Z] ERROR nvme: io 85% lat 6ms -> backlog
[2026-03-15T01:03:14Z] INFO cgroup: writeback started for tenant-87 size=2.1GB
```
emma: running quick checks: iostat + nvme stats on that host. paste in a sec
raj: if tenant-87 is checkpointing, it can saturate queue depth and push streaming tails to p99. Options: throttle tenant IO via cgroup blkio.weight, evict to spare host, or soft-evict (pause new streams).
leo: we have hot spare capacity on pool-5, can migrate a subset of sessions. but migration takes 20-40s per session — might worsen streaming stalls for those sessions.
maria: paging customers: support-bot: Notifying affected accounts: acct-455, acct-661 (both active streams). Support says acct-455 reported intermittent stalls for 2 minutes
oncall: runbook step1: confirm noisy tenant -> step2: try non-disruptive throttle -> step3: if not stable, migrate sessions -> step4: escalate to oncall-sre for host-level remediation
emma: running quick blkio check and dstat now:
```
# blkio controller show for tenant-87
blkio.weight=100 (default)
# iostat -x 1 3
Device:         r/s   w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s  rrqm/s wrqm/s  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1       1800  950  51200  982400 0.00   12.00   9.61   1.20   98.5
```
emma: %util ~98 on nvme, yep IO saturated
raj: try reducing blkio.weight for tenant-87 to 40 for 30s and observe. command:
```
echo 40 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant-87/blkio.weight
```
leo: prepping the command on hgp-03-2 now. applying to all 3 impacted hosts sequentially to avoid global shock
leo: applied on hgp-03-2 -> monitoring
emma: graphs updating, p99 on that host dropped from 1400ms -> 700ms in ~18s
maria: support: acct-455 reports partial improvement but still occasional stall, continuing to monitor
oncall: good, keep throttle for 5m and watch. If p99 < 650ms across pool, keep policy and plan follow-up. If not, escalate to soft-evac
raj: while throttle gives breathing room, we should gate long-term: add IO limit to tenant-87's job spec and open ticket to tenant team to stagger checkpointing windows
leo: telemetry: recording events and tagging host metrics with incident id INC-20260315-017
emma: throttle held for 5m, p99 stabilized to ~420ms across pool, p95 steady at 200ms. removing throttle gradually causes a small rebound; looks like noisy neighbor caused most of it
chris-sre: continuing handoff: I'm taking the incident for night oncall. summary for next shift: noisy neighbor (tenant-87) caused NVMe saturation -> p99 latency spike & streaming stalls; immediate mitigation was blkio.weight throttle to 40 across 3 hosts, reduced p99 from 1420ms to ~420ms. next steps: migrate long-running sessions off shared pool, add permanent IO caps for tenant-87, and schedule deeper host IO tuning.
maria: creating customer impact note for incident channel and pinging account owners for follow-up :email:
support-bot: Customer notification queued: template used "We experienced transient streaming stalls between 01:02-01:12 UTC impacting streamed responses. Mitigation applied; ongoing follow-up planned."
emma: logging commands used and timings into incident doc:
```
- 01:03:30 applied blkio.weight=40 on tenant-87 (hgp-03-2)
- 01:03:45 applied on hgp-03-1
- 01:04:10 applied on hgp-03-5
- 01:09:45 throttle removed to observe behaviour -> partial rebound -> re-applied as policy
```
raj: also found kernel writeback bursts: adding sysctl tweak to limit dirty_bytes temporarily on those hosts as safety net:
```
echo 268435456 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_bytes  # 256MB cap
```
leo: applied dirty_bytes change on all 3 hosts, no adverse effects seen in next 2m
chris-sre: created follow-up tasks: [T1234] add IO cgroup limits to tenant onboarding checklist, [T1235] schedule host NVMe QoS testing, [T1236] consider preemptive session migration policy when util>85%
oncall: tagging severity: sev3 -> customer seen stalls but mitigated within 10m
maria: final notes: write short postmortem stub and assign to eng-infra + tenant ops for root cause and prevention. I'll leave detailed timeline in the incident doc.
emma: before I sign off, small note: if we see recurrent noisy tenants, consider moving heavy checkpoint workloads to dedicated pools as a product offering (again).
chris-sre: thanks team, handoff complete. I'll run a 30m watch and update incident ticket. If anything flares, page me @chris-sre. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-017 created and assigned to chris-sre. status=watching
